title: Non-disruptive passive-promotion certification and restore smoke suite
creator: Ava Chen
description:
Goal: build and run a non-disruptive certification suite for scheduled active->passive failover drills that validates backup/restore integrity, circuit-breaker behavior, and workload-aware load-shedding without cutting live traffic.

Scope:
- Create an automated smoke suite that exercises promotion choreography in a mirror-only mode (traffic shadowing + synthetic canary writes) so we can validate state convergence and SLO behavior without doing an actual cutover.
- Validate backup snapshots, incremental restore, and KV consistency checks across the primary and passive region.
- Profile circuit-breaker tripping thresholds and verify graceful load shedding policy enforcement under staged overloads.
- Produce pass/fail assertions and telemetry artifacts (dashboards, runbook checklist, and post-run report) to certify the standby region for scheduled passive promotion.

Acceptance criteria:
1) Restore sanity: a full restore from the most recent cross-region snapshot and incremental journals results in identical key hashes and head index for 99.99% of sampled keys (per the kv-checker tool).
2) SLO preservation: mirrored traffic + synthetic write load keeps production SLOs (p95 latency and error budget) within target (+/- 3%) during the drill. Any SLO regression must be documented and classified as tolerable/untolerable.
3) Circuit-breaker correctness: CBs in the serving runtime should trip in the expected order (per-route, per-model), and circuit-open fallbacks must route to defined lower-capacity model variants. Tests must assert fallback routes work end-to-end.
4) Load-shedding policy: when simulated load exceeds thresholds, shedding should preserve high-priority routes and shed background/low-priority requests; verify via request traces.
5) Non-destructive: no production writes are lost or committed in a way that affects customer-visible state; all candidate writes should be synthetic and reversible.

Runbook (high-level):
- Pre-run checklist (48-24 hours):
  * Notify customers and stakeholders via DR channel and #oncall (link to stakeholders doc).
  * Ensure latest daily snapshot uploaded to cross-region storage and validate checksum.
  * Schedule a maintenance window and reserve on-call rotation.
  * Provision synthetic canary accounts and test fixtures in both regions (read-only tokens for mirrored path).
  * Confirm telemetry retention flags are set for the drill.
- Pre-flight (T-2 hours):
  * Run snapshot-verify.sh against latest snapshot; capture kv-checksum and sample diffs.
  * Run a dry-run of circuit-breaker thresholds on a staging replica to ensure CB flapping is not present.
  * Load the traffic mirror config in the edge router with shadow-only mode.
- Execution (T+0):
  * Start synthetic canary writer (writes isolated, namespaced keys with time-based suffixes). These writes are directed to the passive region only (no commit to primary).
  * Run incremental-restore smoke: restore incremental journals on the standby to a temporary namespace and run kv-checker.
  * Gradually increase synthetic read/write pressure to trigger load-shedding and CBs; steps at 50%, 75%, 100% of projected peak.
  * Capture traces, span logs, metrics for p50/p95/p99 latencies, error rates, CB open counts, and shed counts.
- Validation (T+30m):
  * Execute automated assertions: kv-checker pass, latency within threshold, CB fallbacks exercised, no driftier-than-allowed keys.
  * If any assertion fails, run rollback steps and collect forensic artifacts (heap/stack dumps, kernel profiles).
- Rollback / Recovery:
  * Disable traffic mirror and synthetic writers.
  * Revert any temporary namespace or test-only service account.
  * If a partial promotion was attempted (should not occur in mirror mode), execute controlled demotion and reconcile with write-ahead/journal replays.
- Post-run (T+24h):
  * Produce a drill report including: test artifacts, time-sequenced telemetry snapshots, list of failures and mitigations, recommended runtime tuning, and estimated customer impact.

Automation & tooling deliverables:
- snapshot-verify.sh — validates snapshot checksums and extracts sample keys (stored in infra/dr-tools).
- kv-checker — deterministic key-hash comparator with sampling knobs and drift scoring (output: pass/fail + score).
- cb-sim-runner — gRPC load harness that can emulate per-route latencies and backend saturation to ensure circuit-breakers behave as configured.
- shed-emulator — synthetic request generator which tags requests with priority labels and enforces shedding policy on the runtime to verify preserved route ratios.
- drill-orchestrator (GitHub: redwood/ops/drill-orchestrator) — orchestrates the sequence above and uploads artifacts to S3.

Telemetry & dashboards (queries to capture during run):
- runtime.latency.{p50,p95,p99} by region, by model
- runtime.errors.count by route and error_type
- cb.state_changes and cb.open_counts by rule_id
- shedding.events and shed_rate by priority_level
- kv.verify.sample_drift_score and restore.duration
- trace: sample end-to-end trace for test synthetic keys

Risk & mitigations:
- Risk: accidental promotion or write mixing. Mitigation: run entirely in mirror mode with network ACLs that prevent write propagation to primary; require human sign-off to flip any promotion knob.
- Risk: telemetry noise masks SLO regressions. Mitigation: set temporary high-fidelity retention and isolate drill tags.
- Risk: circuit-breaker misconfiguration causes large-scale fallback to expensive variants. Mitigation: verify fallback quotas and cost-budgets in the orchestrator before the run.

Deliverables & timeline:
- Week 0: prototype kv-checker and snapshot-verify.
- Week 1: implement cb-sim-runner and shed-emulator; integrate with drill-orchestrator.
- Week 2: internal dry-run against staging; iterate on thresholds.
- Week 3: schedule non-disruptive production certification run and collect artifacts.

Links & artifacts:
- Draft runbook doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/ops/non-disruptive-dr-cert
- Drill orchestrator repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/drill-orchestrator (PRs: #312, #318)
- KV-checker binary + docs: s3://redwood-ops-artifacts/kv-checker/v0.2/README.md

Notes for reviewers:
- The suite intentionally avoids any live failover; the goal is to certify standby readiness in a non-destructive manner and to gather telemetry-driven guidance for safe promotions.
- This ticket pairs with ENG-701234 (follow-on: controlled promotion and rollback rehearsal) which will execute an actual cutover in a narrow maintenance window once this certification passes.
